We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <=9999 (we cannot check price but assume typical). Need to produce JSON route with molecules and reactions with template IDs. We need to find suitable retrosynthetic steps using templates. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates that break certain bonds. The target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's analyze structure: It's a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with para-methyl (toluene) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl which has a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH (anilide). Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH substituent (aniline). So product is fairly complex.

We need retrosynthesis up to 3 steps. Likely disconnections: 1) formation of sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline derivative. 2) formation of amide via coupling of acid chloride with aniline. 3) maybe Wittig or Heck to form the trans-alkene.

Simplify: Could start from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and aniline bearing the rest of chain (i.e., 4-(trans-... ) phenyl sulfonamide). Or we could start from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl with side chain.

Potential route:

Step 1: Couple p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-CH3C6H4SO2Cl) with 4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH (i.e., 4-aminophenyl with side chain). That yields sulfonamide.

Step 2: Form amide: React 4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-COCl (acid chloride) with aniline (Ph-NH2). That gives the amide attached to aniline.

Step 3: Form trans-alkene via Heck coupling of 4-bromo-phenyl-sulfonyl? Actually we need to attach CH=CH-COCl to phenyl. Could start from 4-bromo-phenyl-sulfonyl? Another approach: Use Suzuki coupling to attach phenyl to vinyl group.

Simplify: Use commercially available trans-cinnamic acid (trans-3-phenylacrylic acid) as side chain. Then convert to acid chloride then amidate with aniline (Ph-NH2) to give trans-cinnamoyl anilide (C6H5-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). Then sulfonylate with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride on the aniline? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring (the one bearing the trans-cinnamoyl). Actually target: phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) attached to sulfonyl group (SO2) linking to p-tolyl. The phenyl ring also has the trans-cinnamoyl amide attached at para position? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: Starting from p-tolyl (Cc1ccc...cc1). At para position (relative to methyl) there is NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl has substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position (relative to sulfonyl). So the second phenyl is para-substituted with trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline that also has an NH (i.e., an aniline with an extra NH? Actually Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an NH attached to phenyl (i.e., an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl and also has an H). So it's a primary aniline attached to carbonyl (amide). So the amide is -C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3) and also N attached to something else? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is N attached to phenyl and also has an N at the end? The SMILES: ...C(=O)N c3ccccc3 N . That is an amide nitrogen attached to phenyl (anilide) which also has an NH substituent (i.e., an aniline with an extra NH? Actually the phenyl has an N attached at one position (the amide) and also an N attached at another position? The SMILES "c3ccccc3N" is an aniline (phenyl-NH2). So the amide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl carbon (forming anilide) and that phenyl also has an NH2 substituent (para? not specified). So the amide is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 group (i.e., 4-aminophenyl amide). So the product is a bis-aniline? This is complex.

Nevertheless, we can propose a route using commercially available building blocks: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodo) with trans-cinnamoyl aniline.

Simplify: Use building blocks:

- 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) is commercially available (p-phenylenediamine). Actually p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) has two NH2 groups. That could serve as the phenyl with both amide and sulfonamide attachments (one NH for sulfonamide, one NH for amide). Indeed the target phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) has two substituents: sulfonamide (via N) and trans-cinnamoyl amide (via N attached to carbonyl). So that phenyl is a diamine (p-phenylenediamine) where one NH is sulfonylated, the other is acylated with trans-cinnamoyl (which itself is attached to an aniline). Wait the amide attaches to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the carbonyl attaches to N which is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3) that also has an NH2. So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH2 (i.e., 4-aminophenyl). So the amide is formed between trans-cinnamic acid and 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine). So we need trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and p-phenylenediamine (commercial). Then we need to sulfonylate the other amine of p-phenylenediamine with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial). That yields final product.

Thus steps:

Step 1: Acylation: React trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) with p-phenylenediamine to form amide on one amine, leaving the other amine free. Use coupling reagent (e.g., EDC) but we can assume template for amide formation via acid chloride. So we need trans-cinnamoyl chloride (can be generated from trans-cinnamic acid + SOCl2). But we can treat as commercially available trans-cinnamoyl chloride (maybe not). Simpler: Use trans-cinnamic acid and coupling reagent; but template may be "amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine". We'll search.

Step 2: Sulfonylation: React p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride with the remaining amine of the intermediate to give sulfonamide.

Thus total 2 steps (plus maybe activation). That's within 3 steps.

Now we need to find template IDs for amide formation and sulfonamide formation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken/formed.

Let's search for amide formation: functional_groups_formed: "amide". broken: "carboxylic acid" maybe.
